key_insight: Combining doubly robust estimation with linear programming selects cross-border fulfillment centers that reduce delivery time and logistics cost versus expert-defined policies.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports multi-objective fulfillment routing while keeping the domestic network fixed.
method: Use doubly robust estimation to inform source-center selection.
Apply linear programming to balance delivery time, cost, profit, and shipped units.
evidence_signal: Across three production-scale corridors using 12 months of data, offline replay and shipment-level counterfactual matching showed 8.5–51.1% faster delivery, 4.4–48.3% lower logistics cost, and up to 6.5 percentage-point gains in 5-day/$5 target compliance.
watch_item: Offline counterfactual evaluation does not establish live operational gains; prospective validation is needed before deployment.
paper_title: Cross-Border Fulfillment Center Selection via Doubly Robust Estimation and Linear Programming
